newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Partco expects 13 pct of UK mkt.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Partco expects 13 pct of UK mkt.

text.p: Rapidly-growing British auto parts supplier and distributor Partco Group Plc expects to lift its share of the British market to 13 percent from 8.0 percent after its planned acquisition of Dana Corp's European arm.

The 103 million stg, or $168 million, deal with Dana, sealed earlier on Wednesday, would almost double the company's turnover on an annualised basis, lifting it to 400 million stg, chief executive Peter Redfern said in an interview on Thursday.
"It will get materially earnings enhancing in 1998... there are lots of synergies," he said.
One of the key elements in Dana Distribution Europe is a chain of paint and finishing products stores across Britain called Brown Brothers, which has 135 distribution points.
"Brown Brothers fits superbly into the Partco Group and the acquisition is based on very strong industrial logic," Redfern said, noting it brought with it a market-leading presence.
Other attractive European operations include a strong business in the Netherlands which, in combination with Partco's existing Belgian distribution company, should be a strong base.
"We see the opportunity for getting more horsepower from Benelux is obviously appreciable," he told Reuters.
Even with an increased British market share, and a platform for further organic growth, Redfern said Partco's ambitions to make even bigger inroads in its home market remained.
"There is a lot of growth to go for in the UK," he said.

The company expected the deal will need only 1.5 million stg in extraordinary costs this year, he added, saying that the point of the deal had been to catalyse growth, not shrink or rationalise any businesses.

From a financial point of view, the planned acquisition will have a minor impact on Partco's gearing, lifting it to about 107 percent by the end of this year from just above 100 percent at present. More importantly, Redfern stressed, the company's cash to interest cover would remain well over six times.
The chief executive said he was confident the incoming units would be as cash-generative as existing ones and that the cycle of funding further bolt-on growth from cash could go on.
"That's what it boils down to -- we tend to use our cash to reinvest in the business and grow it," he said, adding, "There's no reason at all to stop".
"What we've got to do is carry through this acquisition and get down to integrating the businesses so we've got a damned good springboard for the next one," Redfern said.
